stance.label: Short-term bearish, spot sold while leverage stepped aside; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: $60,000 gave way to spot selling with no liquidation cascade; leveraged longs left on their own, so the $58,525 low now depends on spot bids.
summary: Short-term bearish: the close slipped back under $60,000 without long liquidations; the selling came from Coinbase spot and the ETFs, and Monday's perp longs were gone within a day. Long-term bullish: the past month's net realized losses broke a cycle-scale threshold, and total unrealized profit is down to 33.2% of market cap. A close below $58,525 is a new low for this cycle; a close back above $64,000 would show the supply is being absorbed.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 13 straight closes below; the close needs +20.7% to get back above

overview.lead: Yesterday we wrote that the longs who chased would be tested next; they left before the test came. Volume was 21% lighter than Monday and price still fell 2.4%.
points: Close $59,741, intraday low $59,197 and high $61,592 (Kraken); volume was 0.79x the prior day and the close sat in the bottom quarter of the day's range.

US stocks split: Nasdaq -1.48%, Dow +0.85%, and Nvidia gave back 5.9%. A report of new tariffs hit futures first, then consumer confidence at 103.3 came in far above forecasts, strengthening the case for a hike.
Fear & Greed 11, day 12 of extreme fear; November is down 22.9% so far, against the worst November since 2013 at -37.0% in 2018.
Nothing new on the exit framework or the market stage; 13 straight closes below the 200-day MA.

cycle.lead: Valuation pressed a little lower: the share of long-term holders at a loss is back at 46%, half a point from this cycle's high, and the miner-capitulation flag went out after one day.
points: The 30-day net realized loss in today's second finding belongs here: this is the third break of the trigger line this cycle, after two near the February and June lows (CoinMetrics, Nov 23).
Long-term holder loss share 46.0%, from 45.0% a day earlier; this cycle's high is 46.5% on Nov 20, and a close below about $58,500 would exceed it (CheckOnChain; the price level is an estimate).

The Hash Ribbons miner-capitulation flag is off: the 30-day hashrate average, 1,013.2 EH/s, is back above the 60-day at 1,012.8 (mempool.space). Yesterday we wrote it had flagged by a hair; it flipped back in a day.

The market stage is still bull, with 6 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA against the 30 the rule needs to exit; none of the 6 evidence lights is on today, as the 90-day change in exchange supply turned to +0.07%.

market.lead: Price has dropped to the lower edge of this cycle's high-volume area near $58,750; only 1.1% of the past year's closes are lower than today's.
points: The selling in today's first finding stretched the down leg to 64 days and -31.0% on a closing basis; the close is 1.6% above the Nov 20 closing low of $58,806.
The close sits at -1.65 standard deviations on the short-term holder cost bands, with -2 standard deviations at $56,479 (Bitview).

Over 7 days the most coins moved into the three $59,000–$61,000 buckets, 400K BTC in all; these freshly moved coins have a cost basis right at the close (Bitview; on-chain moves are not necessarily trades).

The Sell Pressure Index has been maxed for 15 days with momentum at 0.08; this combination occurred 20 times since 2012, with price higher 90 days later in 12 and a median further drop of 12% before the exit.

deriv.lead: Leverage backed out quietly: Monday's chasing longs closed on their own, Hyperliquid flipped to shorts paying, and option money kept buying downside protection.
points: The other half of today's first finding: long liquidations for the whole day were only $56.5M, and the three perp venues were net taker sellers of 656 BTC after net buying 10,873 BTC the day before (Coinalyze).
Weighted funding rate 1.30%, from 4.78% a day earlier; Hyperliquid -10.19%, Binance 2.44%.
Options turned defensive again: 24-hour put volume was 1.70x call volume, from 0.76x a day earlier; DVOL 53.1, 25-delta risk reversal -9.2 (Deribit).

The estimated long-liquidation band now sits just under the close, 14K BTC at $57.3–59.2K (several exchanges, an estimate); estimated dealer gamma is negative at $58,000 and $60,000, so hedging amplifies moves around those strikes (Deribit). The order book shows a $239M bid at $59,000 on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The one piece of good news on the demand page is that stablecoins stopped shrinking for a day; Coinbase taker selling widened to its heaviest since the data begin in August 2021.
points: ETFs lost $570M net on Nov 23, the fifth straight trading day of outflows, with IBIT at $509M (CoinMarketCap, matching Farside); on Farside's count November outflows total $4.71B, past June's $4.51B and a monthly record. Our Nov 20 entry still lacks IBIT.

Coinbase spot was a net taker seller of 6,674 BTC over 7 days, from 4,820 BTC a day earlier (Coinalyze); the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is -0.012%, so the US and offshore gap is small and the selling is on both sides.

Stablecoins $283.2B, up $0.5B on the day and still down 1.1% over 7 days (DefiLlama); USDT at $0.9986, with a 7-day average discount of 0.161%, in the deepest 0.5% since the data begin in October 2022.

The Asian premium faded: the OTC USDT premium is 0.26%, from 0.74% a day earlier, and the Korea premium 1.39%. Rates are unchanged, with Polymarket at 96.0% for a December hike and the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.63%.

onchain.lead: The sellers changed: the short-term holder capitulation cluster ended on day 14, while long-term holder loss-taking kept growing.
points: The sellers in today's first finding: long-term holders realized $4.60B of losses over 7 days, from $4.23B a day earlier; the LTH-SOPR 7-day average, 0.737, is the lowest since Jun 30 (Bitview).

Short-term holder loss intensity fell to 1.83, under the threshold of 2, ending the cluster that began Nov 10; returns after past clusters were about the same as on any other day. STH-SOPR 0.980, below 1 for 19 days (CheckOnChain).

Network-wide realized losses were $1.27B on the day, close to the prior day's $1.32B, against the Nov 20 peak of $2.84B; 26.7% of the last 30 days' realized losses came from coins bought 1–2 years ago (Bitview).

By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 62K BTC over 7 days while the 100–1,000 BTC tier lost 38K BTC (Bitview); the long-term holder 30-day net position is -152K BTC, negative for 112 days (bitcoin-data, Nov 23).

exit.lead: The exit page is empty today; the nearest condition is more than 85% above the close.
points: 13 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $72,130, 17.2% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.415, with the 0.75 line at $110,664; the three top indicators read 8 / 7 / 41, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 23).

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost $569.7M net on Nov 23, the fifth straight trading day of outflows, with IBIT at $509M; November outflows total $4.71B, past June's $4.51B and a monthly record
news.source: CoinDesk, 2026-11-24 (Farside data; Crypto Briefing's same-day figures agree)
news.read: Our data source also shows -$569.7M for Nov 23, so the two agree for that day; our Nov 20 entry is still only -$127M because it lacks IBIT, which leaves the chart's 20-trading-day total of -$4.35B about $0.54B shallower than Farside's count. The largest fund is still the one leading redemptions, on the same day price was pushed back from $64K. ETFs are the biggest piece of the spot selling in today's first finding.

news.title: WSJ: the US could announce new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies as soon as this week, with China's rate the highest and the EU, Japan and South Korea capped at 15%; S&P 500 futures fell as much as 1.25% and the Nasdaq closed down 1.48%
news.source: Investing.com, 2026-11-24 (citing The Wall Street Journal; closing figures from Capp Notes, same day)
news.read: The risk appetite that Nvidia created on Monday was interrupted within a day: the S&P 500 closed down 0.50%, Nvidia gave back 5.86%, and the Dow rose 0.85%. BTC did not follow Monday's rally and still followed Tuesday's drop; over the last 90 US trading days BTC beat the S&P 500 on 47.8% of them. Tariffs are a new source of uncertainty and the final rates are not set. Macro backdrop; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: US consumer confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November against a 92.2 forecast; the New York Fed president called inflation "too high" and one governor argued for a 50 bp hike in December; the 2-year Treasury yield held at 4.63%
news.source: Capp Notes, 2026-11-24 (CoinDesk reported the Fed remarks the same day)
news.read: The stronger the data, the less doubt about a December hike; the debate has moved to 25 or 50 bp. On Polymarket our reading is 96.0% for a hike in December, of which only 2.5% is for 50 bp or more; the 2-year yield is 0.63 points above the Fed's upper bound. Tonight's October PCE is the last major release before the decision. Rates remain a headwind for BTC; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: BTC fell back below $60,000, to about $59,400 intraday, erasing Monday's gain; Strategy common stock fell about 7% to $78.50 after touching $77.89, its lowest since early 2024, and ETH fell about 6%
news.read: Our close is $59,741 with an intraday low of $59,197 (Kraken). Today's first finding breaks this move down: long liquidations were only $56.5M and the selling was spot. We record Strategy holding 851,305 BTC at a paper loss of 20.8%; it pays its preferred dividend by issuing common stock, and the lower the share price, the costlier that route. MSCI removes it from its indexes on Nov 30. For BTC this is a weaker buyer and adds no new selling.

news.title: Glassnode: the drop to $55,000 put a record 11.6M+ BTC at a loss and cut supply in profit to 8.5M BTC, below the 8.6M of the 2022 FTX collapse; over the past 15 days only entities holding 100–10,000 BTC accumulated
news.read: More coins are underwater than at the last bear-market bottom, which is another way of saying long-term cheap. Our supply in profit is 46.3% (bitcoin-data, Nov 23) and relative unrealized profit is 33.2%, below the 35% floor for 11 days. One difference: it counts entities and sees the 100–10,000 BTC group accumulating, while our address-balance tiers show the 100–1,000 BTC tier down 38K BTC over 7 days. The definitions differ and cannot be converted, and we do not describe this as large holders buying.

news.title: South Korea's Financial Services Commission published a draft digital asset act: it lifts the domestic ICO ban in place since 2017, lets bank-majority consortiums issue won stablecoins first, and caps an exchange's major shareholder at 20% (up to 34% with approval)
news.read: Korea is one of Asia's heaviest retail markets, so a legal framework is a long-term positive; the draft still goes to the National Assembly with no timetable. Our Korea premium is 1.39%, with a 7-day average of 2.16% against a median of 1.14%, so Korean buyers were more active than US buyers this week. It brings no immediate money and changes none of our readings.

news.title: Oil rebounded: WTI +2.35% to $82.05 and Brent $91.40 after reported attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz; gold fell 2.64% to $3,555 and the dollar index fell 0.47%
news.read: Yesterday we wrote that falling oil was one of the few variables improving on the rates side; it reversed in a day. Gold fell more than BTC on the same day, and a softer dollar helped neither; over the last two months BTC is down 29.2% and gold 16.9%. The effect on BTC is indirect and changes none of our readings.

actions.head: No action today.
actions.text: No new trigger: the hedge buy-back condition was met on Nov 17, and the MVRV Z 7-day average is 0.27, still below 0.5 (CoinMetrics, Nov 23).

actions.head: Don't read the drop in funding, or Hyperliquid turning negative, as a crowded-short setup for a bounce.
actions.text: Funding fell because Monday's chasing longs closed on their own, on a day when Coinbase taker selling was still widening. The record that "negative funding usually precedes gains" refers to the 7-day average turning negative, with price higher 90 days later in 10 of 13 cases; the 7-day average today is 2.17%.

actions.head: Don't treat the 30-day net realized loss breaking its trigger line as a confirmed bottom.
actions.text: The line says price is near a cycle low: after the breaks of Nov 2018 and May 2022 price still fell another 26% and 46%. This cycle it broke once in February and once in June, and today's close is lower than on either of those days.

actions.head: Tonight's PCE, thin Thanksgiving trading and Friday's expiry (Taipei time).
actions.text: Nov 25 21:30 October PCE, the Q3 GDP revision and jobless claims; Nov 26 03:00 the Beige Book; Nov 26 Thanksgiving, markets closed; Nov 27 16:00 the Deribit monthly expiry, 25.5% of total open interest with max pain at $72,000, and on the same day difficulty is projected to rise 9.0%. The US Trade Representative's findings on new tariffs could come as soon as this week.

actions.head: $58,525 below; $60,000 and $64,000 above.
actions.text: A close below $58,525 is a new low for this cycle and would also push the long-term holder loss share past this cycle's high; the estimated long-liquidation band at $57.3–59.2K is on the way, and below that is the realized price at $53,097 (Bitview). Above, $60,000 carries $104M of asks (Hyperliquid perps), and the $62,000–$64,000 buckets hold 1.08M BTC of short-term holder supply.

actions.head: The next things that would make the framework act are the MVRV 0.75 line at $110,664 and the $125,000 level.
actions.text: They are 85.2% and 109.2% away, both far; the close is 17.2% below the 200-day MA at $72,130.

changes.title: The short-term holder capitulation cluster ended
changes.say: The most recent buyers are selling with less urgency and long-term holders have taken over, with 7-day realized losses up from $4.23B to $4.60B. The selling has a new source and is no smaller.

changes.title: Option volume swung back to puts
changes.say: Two days of cheaper protection stopped today, 3.1 points short of the 50 in the Nov 21 second finding; ahead of Friday's monthly expiry the market is paying for downside cover again.

changes.title: Most of the Asian OTC premium is gone
changes.say: Of last weekend's buyers willing to pay up, only Korea is left; the yuan side is back near par and US spot has not filled the gap.

changes.title: Stablecoins rose for the first time in over a week
changes.say: The contraction slowed and has yet to reverse: supply is still down $17.2B over 30 days, and the Nov 20 second finding needs the 7-day change back inside -0.5%.

changes.title: The close is right on estimated production cost
changes.say: A little lower and miners produce at a loss. Price closed below production cost 14 times before and was higher 30 days later in 13; the worst case, Nov 2018, fell another 16% within 90 days. It marks a cheap level and does not rule out further declines.

findings.title: Spot selling took $60,000: leverage stepped aside first, with no liquidations to blame
findings.lean_why: The selling was real money from spot and the ETFs, with no liquidation cascade to explain it; with leverage gone, only spot bids can defend the prior low, and they have not appeared.
findings.what: The close slipped back under $60,000 on spot selling: long liquidations for the whole day were only $56.5M and the close was $59,741 (Kraken, Coinalyze, Nov 24).
findings.why: Start with which side moved. Derivatives stepped back: the three perp venues were net taker sellers of 656 BTC after net buying 10,873 BTC the day before; the weighted funding rate fell from 4.78% to 1.30% and Hyperliquid flipped to -10.19%; total open interest is 321K BTC, only 0.3% lower over 7 days, so longs left while positions did not shrink and the replacements lean short (Coinalyze). Spot added to its selling: the three spot venues were net taker sellers of 1,897 BTC on the day, from 1,188 BTC a day earlier; Coinbase was a net taker seller of 6,674 BTC over 7 days, the heaviest since the data begin in August 2021; ETFs lost $570M net on Nov 23, the fifth straight trading day of outflows. On-chain data show who sold: long-term holders realized $4.60B of losses over 7 days, from $4.23B a day earlier; short-term holders realized 13,063 BTC of losses against 2,243 BTC of profit on the day (CheckOnChain); 630K BTC changed price bucket over 7 days, of which 430K BTC had a cost basis above the 7-day high and so moved at a loss (Bitview; on-chain moves are not necessarily trades). Some readings point the other way: OKX spot was a net taker buyer of 1,504 BTC on the day (OKX only), stablecoins rose $0.5B in a day, and addresses with 10K+ BTC added 62K BTC over 7 days (mostly exchanges and custodians). All three are still small next to Coinbase and the ETFs.
findings.alt: The other path is that selling is nearly done: the short-term holder capitulation cluster ended on Nov 23, leverage is largely cleared, and if the prior low holds the newly opened shorts have to cover. Coinbase tells the two apart: 7-day net taker selling shrinking to within 3,000 BTC would mean US spot selling is fading. Data limits: taker flow counts aggressive orders only and misses fills against resting orders; Binance's public liquidation feed under-reports and Hyperliquid is absent from the liquidation totals; the Nov 24 ETF figure is not out yet, and our Nov 20 entry still lacks IBIT.
findings.history: When long-term holders also sell at a loss, the following month has usually been poor; when longs take most of the liquidations, price has more often been higher three months on. The LTH-SOPR 7-day average has fallen into its lowest 2% of the past year only 4 times since late 2023, with a median 30-day return of -4.3% against +1.4% for any day. Longs made up 74.9% of the last 30 days' liquidations; of the 7 times that share passed 70%, price was higher 90 days later in 5.
findings.so: What changed is the mechanism for the next move: yesterday the risk sat with the longs who chased, and they have left, which removes a liquidation chain below and also shows no spot buyer is taking this level. What has not changed is the long-term view, with valuation in the bottom zone; the market stage and exit framework did not move.
findings.next: By Dec 1: a close below $58,525 would mean spot selling has taken out the prior low as well; Coinbase 7-day net taker selling shrinking to within 3,000 BTC would mean the selling is fading and this view is refuted.

findings.title: 30-day net realized loss broke the cycle-scale line, the third time this cycle
findings.lean_why: Loss-taking on this scale has only appeared near cycle lows, moving coins to holders with a lower cost basis; it marks the zone, and the loss-taking itself has yet to shrink.
findings.what: This month's loss-taking has reached cycle scale: the 30-day net realized loss totals $18.6B, 1.51% of market cap, and broke the trigger line on Nov 23 (CoinMetrics, Nov 23).
findings.why: The signal list does not carry this item; the basis is the 30-day cumulative net realized profit and loss, where the trigger line is a quarter of the largest 30-day net profit of the prior 4 years, now at -1.44% of market cap. Whose losses are these: of the last 30 days' realized losses, coins held under a month account for 50.1% and coins bought 1–2 years ago for 26.7%, with almost nothing from coins older than two years (Bitview); network-wide realized losses were $10.7B over 7 days, of which long-term holders took $4.60B. Other sources point to the same zone: the aSOPR 7-day average is 0.960, in its lowest 2% of the past year; relative unrealized profit is 33.2%, below the 35% floor for 11 days (Bitview); the one-year cumulative net realized result is -1.08M BTC and has been negative since Jul 17. What differs from a bottom is the pace: net losses were $8.93B over the last 7 days against $6.71B in the 7 before, so they are still growing.
findings.alt: The other path is that this line only marks the middle of a decline: after the breaks of Nov 2018 and May 2022, price fell another 26% and 46% before bottoming. The pace of loss-taking tells the two apart: 7-day net losses back within $4B would mean fewer sellers; a 30-day total beyond -2% of market cap would mean it is still accelerating. Data limits: this is a net figure and understates gross losses; the signal may be duller in the ETF era because ETF shares change hands on the stock market without touching the chain, and this episode is about a quarter of the cycle's largest net profit against roughly 70% in the two prior cycles; the trigger rule was set after seeing this cycle's results.
findings.history: When this line broke, price was near a cycle low each time, though not always at the lowest point. There have been 8 first breaks since 2015 including this one, and in 4 of the 5 before 2023 price was higher a year later. The two earlier breaks this cycle came in Feb 2026 and Jun 2026, at $63,495 and $59,863 on the day.
findings.so: What changed is one more piece of evidence on the long-term side, pointing to the same zone as the unrealized-profit floor and the long-term holder loss share. What has not changed is the short term: loss-taking is still growing and cannot be read as selling exhausted.
findings.next: By Dec 1: a 30-day net loss beyond -2% of market cap would mean this capitulation is still deepening; 7-day net losses back within $4B would mean fewer sellers and would refute the "still growing" part.

followups.title: Sold straight back at the $64K wall: loss-taking spot sold, leverage chased
followups.say: Close $59,741, further from $64,520; the longs who chased were not flushed, with long liquidations at $56.5M for the day, far below $200M, and they closed on their own. Deadline Nov 30.

followups.title: Miner capitulation flagged by a hair: hashrate rose 11% this week; the strain is costs

followups.title: First hurdle at $62–64K: underwater short-term coins wait, and perps did the buying
followups.say: Confirmed: the close of $59,741 is back below $60,000. The bounce stopped at the underwater supply at $62–64K, and the perp longs that drove it were gone a day later.

followups.title: Loss-taking large enough to shrink realized cap: 1.5% of on-chain capital left in a month
followups.say: Realized cap 30-day change -1.63%, a little deeper than -1.52% a day earlier; it has neither returned inside -1% nor broken -2.5%. Deadline Nov 29.

followups.title: $55K flushed leveraged longs; what bought it back is not yet spot demand
followups.say: Coinbase 7-day net taker selling widened to 6,674 BTC, further from turning positive; the close of $59,741 is 2.0% above $58,525. Neither condition is met; deadline Nov 28.

followups.title: The prior low was tested: this loss-taking is larger than at the June bottom
followups.say: Close $59,741, leaning toward the $58,525 side: 2.0% above it and 3.8% below $62,000. Neither condition is met; deadline Nov 27.

followups.title: Buyers are pulling out faster: stablecoin and ETF outflows grew together
followups.say: Stablecoins $283.2B, up $0.5B on the day, with the 7-day change at -1.1%, not yet inside -0.5%; ETFs lost another $570M on Nov 23. Deadline Nov 27.

followups.title: The 200-day MA has turned down, loosening the premise of the bull label
followups.say: Confirmed: 6 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA, which stands at $72,130, 815 lower than 30 days ago. The rule needs 30 such closes to exit the bull stage, so this is a fifth of the way.

research.summary: Glassnode published a new Week On-chain on Nov 24 that calls this the first major capitulation of the bear market, with $58.5K to hold and the realized price at $53.2K below it, the same reading as today's two findings; K33 and CoinShares have nothing newer than last week.

items.title: The Week On-chain: The Canary in the Coal Mine
items.points: Selling intensified after the $62–66K support broke; realized losses are the heaviest since FTX in November 2022, which it calls the first major capitulation of this bear market; ETFs lost $4.3B net over 20 trading days; nearly 90% of the longs between price and the realized price have been liquidated; dealers are short gamma at $58–64K; a daily close below $60K and the June low at $58.5K opens the way to the realized price at $53.2K.
items.meaning: It lines up with our data item by item: our ETF 20-day total is -$4.35B, estimated negative gamma sits at $58,000 and $60,000, and the realized price is $53,097 (Bitview). It says longs are largely cleared, and today we saw only $56.5M of long liquidations; it notes heavy Coinbase taker selling over 30 days, and ours is a net 6,674 BTC sold over 7 days. Its capitulation call is the same event as today's second finding.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 48
items.points: ETF weekly net outflow of $1.7B, the heaviest since early July, with ETF holders' MVRV down to 0.97; futures open interest fell 12% to $29.3B, the lowest since early March; 25-delta skew rose to 17.4%, the highest since mid-July; supply in profit 47.3%, realized cap monthly change -0.93%.
items.meaning: Same direction as ours: buyers pulling out, protection pricier, leverage flushed once. Today our open interest is only 0.3% lower over 7 days while funding fell from 4.78% to 1.30%, so positions held and their direction changed. Its realized cap monthly change is -0.93% against our -1.63%; the definitions differ and we do not subtract one from the other.

items.title: What Comes Next After a New Cycle Low?
items.points: The Nov 21 low of $55,501 was the lowest since September 2024, with seven straight weekly declines; resistance at $61,300 and the short-term holder cost basis at $72,720, realized price $53,200; its base case is a $56,800–$64,900 range into the Nov 27 expiry, with risk skewed to a retest of $55,501.
items.meaning: Its first resistance at $61,300 was not reclaimed on Tuesday, and the close of $59,741 is still inside its range, near the lower edge. Our short-term holder cost basis is $72,410 and realized price $53,097 (Bitview), nearly identical.

items.title: 10x Weekly Crypto Kickoff: $57,300 Reached. Trust the Bounce, but for How Long?
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: its $57,300 target has been reached and a tactical bounce is possible, but the primary trend remains bearish; its BTC trend model turned bearish on Oct 22.
items.meaning: Same direction as our short-term bearish view that bounces do not travel far; Monday's bounce lasted one day. Preview only, so we have not read its evidence.

items.title: Market update - November 20th, 2026
items.points: It treats $60,000 as the key psychological level, with a $60,000–$90,000 range as its base case, and rejects calls for $40,000; the October FOMC minutes were hawkish and a 25 bp December hike is the main scenario; the IBIT bid-ask spread widened to about 17–19 bp.
items.meaning: The lower edge of its range, $60,000, was lost at today's close by 0.4%; the largest bid on the order book also moved down from $60,000 to $59,000 ($239M, Hyperliquid perps). Nothing newer on its list.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: Institutions filing 13Fs added the equivalent of 49,229 BTC in Q3 and hold a record 356,491 BTC, 27.6% of spot BTC funds; advisers and wealth platforms hold 40.5% of that. From quarter-end to Nov 16 the funds' holdings fell by 38,531 BTC.
items.meaning: The wealth clients who entered in Q3 have a cost near $80K and are now underwater as a group; we estimate the close is 24.4% below ETF holders' cost, below it for 13 days, and November's record outflows show part of this group is redeeming.

items.title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
items.points: ETFs took in $6.36B net in Q3 at a flow-weighted entry near $78,300; it wants three straight days of ETF inflows and STH-SOPR back at 1 before looking at $69,400 and $72,700.
items.meaning: None of its conditions has shown up in our data: ETFs have had 5 straight trading days of outflows and STH-SOPR is 0.980, below 1 for 19 days.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC broke below its 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August levels and funding is negative; it argues these readings have matched BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: Its funding condition moved closer again today: the weighted rate is 1.30% and Hyperliquid is already negative, though the 7-day average is still 2.17%. Nothing newer on its list.
